sources: WEDNESDAY Sep 30 2026 RUN (06:15 UTC, pre-US-open; equity/credit fields are Sep 28-29 closes, commodities and FX are live Sep 30 Asia/Europe). HEADLINE: THE OIL SHOCK IS OVER AND THE CREDIT/RATES SHOCK IS NOT. HY OAS BREAKS 300. ICE BofA US High Yield OAS 302bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.02 pct dated Sep 28), through the 300 level flagged as the key watch line in the last two runs. The full sequence is now 268 (Sep 18), 266 (Sep 21), 268 (Sep 22), 273 (Sep 23), 280 (Sep 24), 293 (Sep 25), 302 (Sep 28) - 34bp of uninterrupted widening in six sessions with no retracement. This is the cleanest and most persistent stress signal on the dashboard and it is now widening INTO falling oil, which removes the energy-cost explanation. OIL COLLAPSES: Brent 95.87 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Sep 30), versus 102.67 at yesterday's run - roughly -6.6 pct in a session and the first sub-100 print of this episode. Investing.com has front-month LCO at 96.84 (-1.01 pct, prior close 97.83) on a slightly different contract basis; both agree Brent is now in the mid-90s. Against the EIA spot series that printed 127.84 on Sep 16 and 114.89 on Sep 22, this is a full round-trip of the Hormuz premium in two weeks. The war premium has been priced out. VOL: VIX 16.04 (Cboe, Sep 29 close), essentially unchanged from 16.07 but still up from 14.21 on Sep 22 - equity vol woke up last session and has not gone back to sleep. MOVE carried at 101.82 (Sep 29; TradingView shows 1d +6.06 pct, 5d +6.67 pct, 1m +45.75 pct, YTD +59.18 pct). Bond vol holding above 100 with a 46 pct one-month gain remains the defining feature of this episode. No Sep 30 print available at run time. RATES KEEP BEAR STEEPENING: 2s10s 0.37 (YCharts, Sep 29), up from 0.32 on Sep 28 and 0.25 on Sep 22 - 12bp of steepening in five sessions. US 10y 5.24 pct (TradingEconomics, Sep 30), down 1bp on the day but up nearly 46bp in September alone and at levels last seen in mid-2007. TradingEconomics notes markets now price close to a full percentage point of Fed HIKES over the next twelve months. BREAKEVENS STILL FLAT - AND NOW THE POINT IS SHARPER: 5y5y forward 2.35 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Sep 28) versus 2.34 on Sep 22 and 2.34 on Sep 25. Oil has fallen 7 pct and long-run inflation expectations did not move; they also did not move when oil was at 128. The long-end selloff is a term-premium and fiscal/supply event, full stop. This remains the single most important line on the dashboard, and today's oil collapse is the cleanest test it has passed. DOLLAR: DXY 101.26 (TradingEconomics, Sep 30), -0.06 pct on the day but +1.91 pct on the month and near the year-to-date high. Trend up on the week. COPPER/GOLD 1.58 - flat for a fourth run. Copper 6.59 USD/Lbs (+0.69 pct) and gold 4,175.47 USD/t.oz (-0.15 pct), both TradingEconomics Sep 30; 6.59/4175.47*1000 = 1.578. Gold holding above 4,100 while oil collapses is itself a signal that the bid is about rates and fiscal risk, not commodities. NFCI -0.56 for the week ending Sep 18 (Chicago Fed via FRED), CARRIED - the Sep 25 print releases today at 08:30 ET / 12:30 UTC, after this run. That print is the first hard read on whether six sessions of credit widening and a 100-plus MOVE have reached broad financial conditions; the index was at the loosest level of the cycle going in. Global liquidity 1 (stable). CARRIED, no new releases: initial claims 197k (week ending Sep 19, DOL via FRED ICSA, next Oct 1), ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, eighth straight expansion month, next Oct 1), UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, four-month low versus 51.7 in August, trend down), building permits 1,403k (August, -2.1 pct m/m, Census/HUD via FRED PERMIT, next Oct 17), LEI y/y about -0.7 pct (Conference Board, August level 99.5), Sahm rule -0.07 (August, FRED SAHMREALTIME, next Oct 2), SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis -10bp (standing assumptions, no free live source). BDTI DATA FLAG - TENTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. Investing.com remains frozen at 1,107 dated 31/03, MacroMicro and Barchart are gated, the Baltic Exchange is subscription-only, and the Exchange's own Circular 44/26 consultation on amending or suspending its Middle East Gulf tanker benchmarks over Hormuz security risk means even a live feed would be of doubtful comparability. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. PICTURE: yesterday the question was whether the market had stopped trading an oil shock and started trading a Fed/term-premium shock. Today it is answered. Brent fell almost 7 pct and gave back the entire war premium; credit spreads widened anyway, through 300; the curve bear-steepened anyway; the dollar held near its high anyway; and 5y5y breakevens sat at 2.35 through all of it. Nothing that was supposed to be caused by oil has reversed with oil. What is left is a rates and fiscal repricing with a hiking Fed priced in, soft domestic data (UMich 48.1, LEI negative y/y, permits falling) and a labour market that has not cracked yet (claims 197k). That is policy-error geometry with the energy alibi removed. WATCH: NFCI today 12:30 UTC (the key release - does credit stress show up in broad conditions), ISM manufacturing and initial claims Oct 1, Sahm rule Oct 2, whether HY OAS keeps widening now that 300 is broken, whether MOVE holds above 100, and whether the 10y takes 5.30. SOURCES: FRED/St. Louis Fed (BAMLH0A0HYM2 Sep 28, T5YIFR Sep 28, NFCI Sep 18, ICSA Sep 19, PERMIT Aug, SAHMREALTIME Aug), YCharts (10-2 Treasury spread Sep 29), Cboe (VIX Sep 29), TradingView ICE-MOVE (MOVE percentage changes, Sep 29 basis), TradingEconomics (Brent, copper, gold, DXY, US 10y - all Sep 30), Investing.com (Brent front-month cross-check Sep 30), Benzinga Sep 29 (MOVE above 100), Conference Board (August LEI), ISM (August manufacturing PMI), Chicago Fed, US Department of Labor, Census Bureau/HUD, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers.
